title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 58
paragraphs: Now these Phoenicians who came with Cadmus, of whom the Gephyraeans were a part, brought with them into the land of Boeotia, when they settled there, many arts, and especially letters, which did not exist, it seems to me, among the Hellenes before this time. At first they introduced the letters used by the Phoenician race generally; but in time, as they changed their speech, they also changed the form of the letters. In most of the places where they lived, the Ionians were the Hellenic people living nearest them; and these, having received the letters by the Phoenicians' instruction, altered their form slightly and so made use of them, and in doing so they called them “phoenicians,” as was only fair, since the Phoenicians had introduced them into Hellas. The Ionians too from ancient times call paper “skins,” because formerly, when paper was scarce, they used goat- and sheep-skins; and even in my own day many of the barbarians write on such skins.
